newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian GIB H1 '96 profit soars.
newsitem.headline: Belgian GIB H1 '96 profit soars.

text.p: (in billions of Belgian francs unless stated)

NOTE - GIB, Belgium's second-largest retail group in terms of consolidated turnover, noted consolidation parameters were not comparable as the 1995 figures included its former U.S. DIY unit Handy Andy.
NOTE - GIB said in a statement the previously-announced capital gain came from the sale of its minority stake in UK DIY chain Homebase.

Super- and hypermarkets: GB Supermarkets ' turnover rose by two percent as against first half 1995, with a three-percent rise in sales in food products. Productivity gains at GB, which is undergoing restructuring, translated into a "reinforced aggressive marketing policy". By the end of the year GB would have renovated or enlarged 15 stores.
The GB division had consolidated its market share and improved its results.

Home-improvement: Turnover at the units in Belgium, France, Spain and Portugal rose by 1.4 percent in the first half. Gardening sales in Belgium and France suffered from poor weather. In Belgium turnover rose by 0.9 percent. In France turnover at the Obi chain rose by 1.2 percent. In Spain turnover rose by 4.4 percent.
Turnover at U.S. division Scotty's climbed by six percent on the year-ago period, boosted by sales to professionals. Operating cashflow was higher.
Scotty's continued its policy of opening small stores, with five new hardware shops so far this year and 17 more on the cards by the end of the year.

Restaurants: GIB was confident that despite disappointing results at beefburger-chain Quick Restaurants - in which GIB has a 57.44-percent stake - the fast-food market still had all its potential for development. Quick had already announced sales rose only by 11.8 percent in the first half, less than previously expected, as a result of the "mad cow" scare. GIB said new products had been introduced to encourage customers to return.
In the first half, 22 new restaurants were opened and 38 would be opened in the second half.
Quick expects brand sales up between 10 and 12 percent for the year.

Speciality retailing: Club, PVC and Disport saw sales rise by four, nine and 18 percent respectively. Inno 's sales rose by three percent. Sarma 's re-positioning plan continued, involving the closure of seven shops. It had a large negative influence on operating cashflow.
